audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer labels the lane HARD while its own diffRating is 4/10 — the label and the number say opposite things.
audit.why: 4/10 is an easy-to-even lane, not a hard one, and Emerald+ 51.06%... in fact 50.3% over 658 games is the definition of even. The mirror page audits/top/nasus__jayce.json was corrected to diff EVEN at 6/10 for Nasus; the inverse of that is EVEN at 4/10 for Jayce. Leaving HARD on a 4/10 page makes the two directions disagree and mirror-fix.js will overwrite it anyway.
audit.corrected: diff EVEN, keeping diffRating 4/10 as the inverse of the mirror's 6/10.

audit.why: The spike ladder is right and matches the mirror: Jayce owns 1-3 on gate-Q, the lane flattens at 4-5 when Wither and a real stack count exist, Level 6 is a non-spike for Jayce because his R is the stance-swap he already had while Fury of the Sands adds Health, attack range and a reduced Siphoning Strike cooldown, and 2+ items is Nasus's. Both charts already read Jayce,Jayce,Jayce,Skill,Skill,Nasus,Nasus, which is exactly the mirror's corrected chart.

audit.whatIsWrong: `spikes[0].text` and `early` both say the Armor/MR shred comes off 'the cannon-to-hammer swap' / 'a Cannon-to-Hammer swap'. The direction is backwards.
audit.why: Riot: from Hammer Stance the R transforms into Mercury Cannon and 'the first attack in this form reduces the target's Armor and Magic Resist'; from Cannon Stance it becomes Mercury Hammer and that first attack 'deals additional magic damage'. The shred is therefore the first attack after swapping INTO Cannon. This matters more here than in most lanes, because the natural Jayce instinct against a melee stacker is to swap to Hammer to fight him — a player following the page shreds nothing on the exact commit they were told to shred on. The mirror audit flagged the identical error from Nasus's side.
audit.corrected: The shred is the first attack after swapping into Mercury Cannon; the Hammer first hit is bonus magic damage.

audit.whatIsWrong: Thundering Blow is mentioned twice, only as a knockback that denies a stack. Its damage type and scaling are never given, and they are the whole reason it is good here.
audit.why: Thundering Blow deals magic damage scaled off the target's MAXIMUM health before the knockback. Nasus's two defensive levers both work against him on that hit: he builds Health, and Fury of the Sands grants bonus Health on top, so the fatter he gets the more this takes off him. It is magic damage, so the armour he stacks does nothing to it. The mirror page states this from Nasus's side; the Jayce side never mentions it, which means the player is told to spend a 20-second cooldown on repositioning when it is also his best single hit into a health-stacker.
audit.corrected: Thundering Blow is magic damage off his MAXIMUM health — Fury of the Sands' bonus Health makes it hit harder, and his armour does nothing to it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Wither is called 'his W' and treated as a permanent condition — no cooldown, so 'trade only while Wither is on cooldown' is unactionable.
audit.why: Wither is 15/14/13/12/11 at 700 range. Fifteen seconds at rank 1 is a real window: once he burns it you have roughly a dozen seconds where the Hextech Capacitor swap speed works and the Hammer commit is safe. Thundering Blow at 20/18/16/14/12/10 is the longer of the two, so the honest sequencing rule is that you trade inside Wither's downtime but you only get one commit per Thundering Blow. Neither number is on the page.
audit.corrected: Wither 15s at rank 1, 700 range; Thundering Blow 20s at rank 1 — commit inside the Wither gap, once per knockback.

audit.whatIsWrong: `spikes[3].text`, `mid`, `late` and `whys[4]` all say Fury of the Sands grants 'lifesteal, size, and bonus resists'. None of those three is in the ability.
audit.why: Riot's Fury of the Sands: a sandstorm that batters nearby enemies, and 'While the storm rages, he gains increased Health, Attack Range, damages nearby enemies, has a reduced cooldown on Siphoning Strike'. No lifesteal, no resistances. His lifesteal is Soul Eater, the passive, which is always on and is not a Level 6 spike at all. The correction changes the advice: bonus HEALTH is exactly what makes Thundering Blow's max-health magic damage hit harder, so his ult makes him a better target for your one commit rather than a tankier one, and the reduced Siphoning Strike cooldown is the real threat to respect.
audit.corrected: Bonus Health, attack range and a faster Siphoning Strike — no resistances, and the lifesteal is Soul Eater, on from Level 1.

edits.before: E (Acceleration Gate) unlocks: a gate-Q Shock Blast detonates on him at huge range and bonus damage, and the cannon-to-hammer swap shreds his Armor/MR on the first hit as he steps up to last-hit a Q stack.
edits.after: E (Acceleration Gate) unlocks: a gate-Q Shock Blast detonates on him at huge range and bonus damage, and swapping INTO Mercury Cannon shreds his Armor/MR on that first attack as he steps up for a Q stack.

edits.before: Levels 1-3 are Jayce's to bully, but don't overstay. At Level 1 he only has one Cannon-Q, so poke Nasus's last-hits and respect that both champs are weak here. The lane turns at 2-3 when E (Acceleration Gate) comes up: fire Shock Blast through the gate for full-range chunk damage, and the first hit after a Cannon-to-Hammer swap shreds his Armor and MR, so every time he walks up to stack Q you get a free trade. Use E Thundering Blow to knock him off the wave and deny those stacks before they snowball.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 are yours to bully, but don't overstay. At Level 1 you have only one Cannon-Q, so poke his last-hits and respect that both champs are weak here. The lane turns at 2-3 when Acceleration Gate comes up: fire Shock Blast through the gate for full-range chunk damage, and the first attack after swapping INTO Mercury Cannon shreds his Armor and MR, so every walk-up for a Q stack is a free trade. Thundering Blow knocks him off the wave and denies the stack before it snowballs.

edits.after: Wither (15s at rank 1, 700 range) eats the Hextech Capacitor swap speed you kite with — inside those 15 seconds of downtime the Hammer commit is safe, outside them it is not.

edits.after: Trade in Wither's 15s downtime, and Thundering Blow him off the wave — it is magic damage off his MAXIMUM health, so his armour and R Health do nothing

edits.after: - Nasus Wither: 15s at rank 1, 700 range — it kills your swap speed, so commit only inside its downtime. - Thundering Blow: 20s at rank 1, magic damage off his MAXIMUM health, then the knockback. One commit per cast.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Wither is 15s at rank 1 — trade inside the gap, never into it.

edits.after: A free-farmed Nasus has hundreds of Q stacks, and Fury of the Sands adds Health, attack range and a faster Siphoning Strike, so one Wither pins you in melee and an empowered Q chunks you.

notes: Full-layer diff was HARD against its own diffRating of 4/10; corrected to EVEN so it matches both the number and the mirror page (audits/top/nasus__jayce.json, corrected to EVEN 6/10 for Nasus). Level charts already agree in both directions and both layers, so I changed no phase sides. One thing I could not verify from the kit files and therefore left alone: `spikes[3].text` claims Fury of the Sands grants 'lifesteal, size, and bonus resists'. Riot's own text gives increased Health, increased Attack Range, nearby damage and a reduced Siphoning Strike cooldown — no lifesteal and no resistances. The lifesteal in his kit is Soul Eater (passive), not R. I did not rewrite it because the same claim appears in `mid`, `late` and `whys[4]` and correcting one without the others would leave the page contradicting itself — see questionsForUser.
